patterns: AI-scare headlines from rawsalerts topped the whole board: banks finding 'rogue AI agents living' in customer accounts (~1.89M, 0.8% likes), an Australian arrested after telling Anthropic's Claude he wanted to attack a daycare (~848k), and the UK telling citizens to stockpile 3 days of food for an AI outage (~197k). Four AI posts pulled ~2.95M views, but like rates stayed around 1%, so they spread on fear and shares rather than agreement

Real-voter clips from Trump's Iowa and South Carolina rallies carried Gunther's day: the farm-family voter explaining the Senate race (~360k), the young Sioux City voter shrugging off gas prices (~258k, 7.7%), and SC rally voters (~52k); 14 rally/Iowa hits, ~575k views

Ilhan Omar's name became the new cycle: 25 hits and ~764k views, driven by the DOJ filing naming her 'Ilhan Nur Said Elmi' (~48k), Trump saying she used a fake name to be sworn in (alx ~35k), and short demands like 'Prosecute. Convict. Deport.' (~52k at 16.7% likes) and 'remove her from Congress' (~42k, 12.2%)

Patriotic-symbol outrage converts: the Iwo Jima statue sledgehammered at Quantico (~122k, 7.8%; follow-up 'Nearly 7,000 Americans died taking Iwo Jima' ~46k, 11.2%) and Tom Skerritt's career tribute (~179k, 10.8%)
Sports-as-culture-war kept punching above its weight: 'LeBron is trash' (~115k, 11.4%), the anthem take (~43k, 12.5%), WNBA boycott (~57k); 10 hits, ~451k views

Election-integrity stories with a named villain: NYT pulling 15 fake Wedgewood polls (~102k, 9.7%), Hobbs canvassers caught on video willing to register non-citizens (~79k), and a federal judge blocking DHS noncitizen-voter checks in nine states (~47k)

Short one-line verdicts again had the best like rates: Rubio son of Cuban exiles (18.0%), Omar 'Prosecute. Convict. Deport.' (16.7%), Somali refugees take (16.1%), 'most corrupt Democrat Party in history' (13.7%)
Ask-@Grok posts still pull views but not engagement: nine of them drew ~427k combined (muscle car ~119k, generations ~93k) at only 0.3-0.8% likes; a good reach tool, a weak loyalty tool
virals_narrative: The outsider AI sweep (last ~48h, two searches, 50 posts) was thin again: X's search ignored the likes filter, so most results were small accounts and auto-generated digests. The useful signal backed up the watchlist's biggest story: @shanaka86 (~10.6k views) pointed out that Axios named JPMorgan, Bank of America and Wells Fargo as racing to contain AI-agent risks but did not say which banks actually found anything, which is a softer story than the 'rogue agents living in accounts' headline. Other recurring threads were Walmart opening a portal for AI agents to shop and pay, a wave of always-on AI assistants (Anthropic's newly announced Claude Duet, Meta Muse, OpenAI Dots), @testingcatalog's daily brief on critical PHP security fixes (~22k), and Ukraine registering an 'AI political party.'
narrative_synthesis: AI fear won the window on raw reach: three rawsalerts AI headlines took ~2.9M views, almost a third of the day, though at low like rates. Gunther's base ran on real-voter rally clips, the Ilhan Omar name story, and patriotic-symbol outrage like the Iwo Jima statue. The open angles are a calm, practical take on AI and your money, honoring the Iwo Jima memorial with the actual history, the fake-poll scandal as a lesson in trusting polls, and the kid who stood up in the Florida cafeteria.
